cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
For normal renal function (eGFR >=90), the starting dose is 50 mg OD, the maximum is 100 mg/day, and monitoring is routine [E2]. For mild renal impairment (eGFR 60-89), the starting dose is 50 mg OD, the maximum is 100 mg/day, and monitoring is routine [E2]. For moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59), the starting dose is 25 mg OD, the maximum is 50 mg/day, and monitoring is recheck 2-4 weeks [E1, E2, E3]. For severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-29), the starting dose is specialist review, the maximum is 25 mg/day, and monitoring is enhanced [E2].

cases.question: What does SB-AX17-2026-09 require?
cases.answer:
SB-AX17-2026-09 requires temporary hepatic monitoring enhancement, with baseline hepatic laboratory values and repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. For ALT/AST >3x ULN, medical review is required [E2]; for Bilirubin >2x ULN, urgent review is required [E2]; and for mild isolated changes below trigger, a repeat test is required [E2]. The bulletin does not change the approved German renal starting dose of 25 mg once daily for moderate renal impairment [E1].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In HN-204, AX-17 adverse event rates are 12.7% for nausea [E1], 14.0% for headache [E1], 15.3% for fatigue [E1], 16.6% for dizziness [E1], 17.8% for rash [E1], and 19.1% for transaminase elevation [E1]. Control rates are 6.0% for nausea [E1], 6.6% for headache [E1], 7.2% for fatigue [E1], 7.8% for dizziness [E1], 8.4% for rash [E1], and 9.0% for transaminase elevation [E1]. Transaminase elevation is serious [E1], while nausea, headache, fatigue, dizziness, and rash are not serious [E1]. The highest treatment % in HN-204 is transaminase elevation (19.1) [E4]. In HN-311, AX-17 adverse event rates are 11.8% for nausea [E2], 13.0% for headache [E2], 14.2% for fatigue [E2], 15.4% for dizziness [E2], 16.6% for rash [E2], and 17.7% for transaminase elevation [E2]. Control rates are 6.0% for nausea [E2], 6.6% for headache [E2], 7.2% for fatigue [E2], 7.8% for dizziness [E2], 8.4% for rash [E2], and 9.0% for transaminase elevation [E2]. Transaminase elevation is serious [E2], while nausea, headache, fatigue, dizziness, and rash are not serious [E2]. The highest treatment % in HN-311 is transaminase elevation (17.7) [E4]. Treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) are -0.9 points for nausea [E4], -1.0 points for headache [E4], -1.1 points for fatigue [E4], -1.2 points for dizziness [E4], -1.2 points for rash [E4], and -1.4 points for transaminase elevation [E4], with control % differences of +0.0 points [E4]. All treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) lie between -1.4 and -0.9 points [E4].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E2] HN-311 · HN-311 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2026-01-18 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-311_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E4] computed by code from [E3] (differences and highest values; not document text)

Descriptive comparison across separate studies, not a head-to-head result.
